table_contract: NodeId is a uint32_t indexing identifier. Graph node creation assigns increasing IDs; representation must handle later graph growth.
Get returns const T&. Missing entries return a shared def_value_ reference. A reference returned for a missing entry must remain the shared default even if that node is later assigned.
Set of a missing default value does not create an entry. Once an entry exists, assigning the default preserves its storage and references.

State contains a PersistentMap<Variable, Node*> (tree, default value, zone). Its constructor requires a Zone; it has operator!= and no default constructor. Copies share immutable persistent tree structure.
Growing ZoneVector<T> directly can invalidate references. Separate chunks or individually allocated values preserve stored-reference stability.
Observed callers consume or copy Get results immediately, but the storage experiment must preserve the stronger existing reference contract.
merge_invariants: MergeInputs reads the predecessor states and old effect-phi state. Scope::~Scope writes the resulting table state only after MergeInputs returns.
Inside MergeInputs, writes affect result PersistentMap or value-phi inputs. Effect-phi inputs are not rewritten.
EffectGraphReducer::Revisit and AddRoot update marks and queue work; neither calls the reducer recursively. There is no reentrant MergeInputs while a cached buffer is in use.
TickAndMaybeEnterSafepoint retains its position inside the variable loop. It handles GC coordination, not concurrent mutation of the private compiler graph or state table.
If lookup counts justify caching, copy State values once per merge, reuse a ZoneVector buffer and avoid loading additional inputs for an empty first state.
diagnostic_lifetime: Print after ReduceGraph and again after EscapeAnalysisReducer::VerifyReplacement. The latter includes replacement and deoptimization-state reconstruction. The zone-allocated tracker destructor is not a reliable flush point.
test_targets: Sparse table defaults, sparse/high IDs, stable stored and missing references, overwriting defaults, non-default-constructible values and allocation-free missing operations.

Existing escape-analysis tests cover loops, phi types, cycles, replacement, frame-state branchpoints, materialization and deoptimization. Run these alongside GraphReducer, LoopPeeling, LoadElimination and DataView checks.
